1#א: Only d'rabbanan. See siman 102 seif 8, where I wrote that even in a doubtful d'rabbanan prohibition there is stringency regarding something that has a permitted aspect specifically, and not regarding other things that are not nullified.
1#ב: And if it is a doubt whether it is worthy of honor, etc. For this stringency that a piece worthy of honor is not nullified is d'rabbanan. And see what I wrote at the beginning of siman 100.
2#א: And basar b'chalav. Because both of them became one body, and the proof is that one receives lashes from the Torah even if one ate only approximately half an olive-measure of milk and half an olive-measure of meat.
2#ב: Because it absorbed taste, etc. For that which is absorbed is not worthy of honor. Based on this, Darkei Moshe and Torat Chatat general rule 40 wrote that cheese curdled in treifah milk that became mixed is not a piece worthy of honor, since the prohibition within it is absorbed, and not like Or Zarua at all — so is rule 5, where he was stringent also in this cheese on the grounds that it is as if born in prohibition. And Maharshal, may his memory be blessed, was puzzled at the Rav Rama in the Torat Chatat, for there in general rule 43 he ruled regarding cheese of a non-Jew that a double doubt does not help, since the prohibition is on account of itself, etc.; and based on this he ruled here too like Or Zarua that it is worthy of honor. And to me it appears that there it deals with cheese of a non-Jew in which there is concern that impure milk became mixed in, and there was no nullification in a majority of kosher items, and it teaches us that regarding double doubt they were stringent because, although all cheeses of non-Jews were forbidden from the outset on account of a d'oraisa doubt, as explained in Or Zarua general rule 26 at its beginning — this is why he calls it a prohibition on account of itself, meaning a certain prohibition, and it has no permission through a double doubt; for if from one doubt alone it is obvious that it is forbidden even though it is d'rabbanan, since there is concern that impure milk became mixed in and there would be a d'oraisa doubt, and even through a double doubt it is not permitted, for the first doubt is counted as certain, since the essence of the d'rabbanan prohibition here was in place of a d'oraisa doubt — and he did not mention worthy of honor at all. But here, where it was curdled in treifah milk and mixed in a majority — meaning that it could be permitted through nullification in a majority of kosher items, but you come to prohibit it on account of worthy of honor — in this I say: since it is absorbed, meaning that there is no mixture of treifah milk as a prohibition in it, but only that it was curdled in it — therefore it was only absorbed and is nullified, as will be explained shortly regarding the distinction between curdling in treifah milk versus treifah milk mixed in. And Maharshal wrote in chapter 25 siman 48, and this is the language of Mordechai in the name of Rabbeinu Shimshon son of Rabbeinu Avraham: who knows whether cheeses are as important as a piece worthy of honor, etc. And to me it appears that certainly there a piece worthy of honor does not apply to cheeses, for if it is moist it is not important, and even dry cheese that is important in our time — nevertheless it is not so important to eat enough for satiety, for it is hard on the body, and especially since many people do not eat it even under duress — until here his language. And his words do not seem right to me in my humble opinion, for we say in the chapter of Rabbi Eliezer that cheese even one day old is fit, and so wrote the long Torat HaBayit regarding cheese made from a treifah animal, which Beit Yosef brought in siman 21, that cheese is worthy of honor; and so explained the Rama in siman 81. Nevertheless, specifically there where the prohibition was on account of itself, for treifah animal milk was mixed in there and it was absorbed — it is worthy of honor; but in cheese absorbed from the prohibition we mentioned through curdling in treifah milk, the words of the Torat Chatat are correct that it was not a piece worthy of honor; and likewise in a mixture of impure milk — it is also not worthy of honor, for the Tur wrote in siman 115 regarding the reason for the prohibition of cheeses of non-Jews: perhaps they mixed impure milk in it, even though no impure milk is actually found — we are concerned that a little remains between its holes — end of his words. And it is obvious that regarding that milk between the holes it is not worthy of honor, since the body of the cheese is not made from it, unlike a mixture of treifah milk. And why did the Torat Chatat mention in general rule 43 "perhaps impure milk was mixed in," and a double doubt does not help, and he did not mention there regarding its being worthy of honor for the matter that nullification in the majority does not help — for there it would certainly be nullified if there is a majority, since it is only like absorbed. Nevertheless it appears to me that ordinary cheese of a non-Jew that was mixed among kosher cheeses we consider as an absorbed prohibition and it is nullified, and we do not say it comes from treifah animal milk, for we follow the majority, and most animals are kosher. And proof: many reasons are stated in the chapter Ein Ma'amidin why they forbade cheeses of non-Jews, as the Beit Yosef brought in siman 115, and he did not mention this reason that it is made from treifah, only "perhaps they mixed impure milk in it" — and this was not worthy of honor, and its law is like an absorbed prohibition as we said. However, one reason he counted there is that they curdle it in the skin of a neveilah stomach — and based on this it has the status of worthy of honor, for there is a meat-and-milk prohibition here. End of my words: in a place where it is known that they do not curdle in the skin of a non-Jew's animal, it is not a piece worthy of honor — so it appears to me.
3#א: And there are those who disagree in all of this. Explanation: and it is reasonable to them that what they said "worthy of honor" does not mean that it must be worthy as it is now, but because of its measure they mentioned it — that it is large like this, worthy to give before a guest after it is cooked.
3#ב: Except for a chicken in its feathers. Because it lacks a great preparation — it implies that if they already removed the feathers but have not yet taken out the innards and opened the belly, this is not considered lacking preparation and it is not nullified. And a sheep whose skin was not removed — it is obvious that it is nullified, a fortiori from chicken feathers; and so Maharshal.
3#ג: But if they were already singed. Even though their hooves were not removed, one can trim them and it is not considered lacking great preparation.
3#ד: Head of poultry. Maharshal wrote in the chapter of Gid HaNasheh siman 53 that the head of an animal is not considered, only the head of a calf — and certainly the tongue of an ox is considered, for Abraham honored the angels with three tongues.
4#א: Fat of the stomach lining, etc. Maharshal wrote there in that siman that the outer membrane of a calf's stomach is considered, although other intestinal organs are not considered; and the Shulchan Aruch already wrote at the beginning of siman 110 that everything depends on place and time, and among us the outer membrane of a calf's stomach is important.
4#ב: But the skin of goose fat, etc. In Or Zarua there in the gloss he brings that if the goose skin was cut into strips its significance is lost. Maharshal was puzzled there: since if cut it is not important, from what aspect would it be important when whole, etc.; and also in my humble opinion the opposite is astonishing, for the main honor is in the goose skin after they cut it into pieces for frying — our eyes see that in every place they honor important people with those fried pieces. End of my words: certainly it is a piece worthy of honor even when cut. And it appears therefore that the Rama did not bring in the Shulchan Aruch, and in Darkei Moshe, this distinction, although the Torat Chatat brought it — it is not the main point, and one may not be lenient in this — so it appears to me.
5#_: Gizzard, etc. Maharshal wrote in the chapter of Gid HaNasheh siman 50, and this is his language: however, it appears to me that in most places I have seen that the gizzard of a goose is considered worthy of honor, and since the Rambam wrote that everything depends on time, certainly a goose gizzard is important and is not nullified — end of his words. It implies that of a chicken it is not worthy of honor; and so in Maharil in the name of Mohar R. Yaakov Tevel — this distinction. And see what I wrote in siman 75 that specifically for this purpose the gizzard is included among intestinal organs, as the Tur's words. Maharshal wrote there, and this is his language: the sages of Krakow ruled on goose meat on the breast called bilak — even though the goose was plucked, nevertheless the bilak is called worthy of honor. And to me it appears they ruled not according to law, although in truth in those places it is fit to honor guests with its roast; nevertheless, since the goose was plucked and its glory removed, its significance was lost, and it is somewhat like a beriah from which a little was removed — its significance is nullified. And here its significance is not nullified, since when it was not plucked it was very important — end of his words. And I wonder whether these words came from Maharshal's mouth, for they are very puzzling: that in a very large and important piece, if a little was cut from it, shall we say its significance was lost? Yet we say in the next seif that significance is not lost through crushing or cutting until its form is lost, etc. And this is not comparable to beriah, for whenever something is removed from it, it is no longer a beriah upon it. Therefore one may not rely on this for practice, only as the sages of Krakow ruled — that any piece currently fit to honor, even though it was formerly more important. It is written in the Levush that those goose livers that turned white from the fat are certainly important and are not nullified.
6#_: And there is no distinction whether they were mixed in their kind. Explanation: regarding something that has a permitted aspect in siman 102 we say that not in its kind — even regarding something that has a permitted aspect — is nullified; and Or Zarua wrote in general rule 25 that a fortiori regarding other things that are not nullified, such as beriah and a piece worthy of honor, their doubt is permitted, as the Shulchan Aruch wrote at the beginning of siman 100, that if they were mixed not in their kind their importance does not help and they are nullified. And he disagrees with the Rama, for Rashba and the Shulchan Aruch in siman 100 regarding a pot of vegetables in which a beriah was lost — everything is forbidden — from which we learn that even not in its kind beriah is not nullified. And in truth his own words contradict one another, for in general rule 43 he wrote many laws regarding worms that forbid in mixtures, and the Torat Chatat wrote in general rule 40 that something that has a permitted aspect is different, for the importance is not on account of the prohibition itself but because there will later be permission for it — the Sages did not want it nullified; and everything mixed not in its kind — the permission is not called on the forbidden item but on the name of the item it was mixed into, and it is as if it has no permission — end of his words. And in siman 102 seif 1 I wrote in the name of Ran a more correct reason. Nevertheless I do not know how this hagahah applies here regarding crushing and nullifying the piece through cutting; and it appears there is a scribal error here, and its place is at the head of the siman in what the Shulchan Aruch wrote that it is not nullified — and here it has no place at all.
7#א: If it is of the forbidden, all of them are permitted. And its explanation appears to be: if you wish to say that the forbidden item also enters into this doubt that perhaps it was cut. And Or Zarua wrote in general rule 25 that this law is only when there are sixty in the prohibition against the heter.
7#ב: One may not rely to say, etc. Even though in every place we follow the majority, here it appears we should say the opposite: everything that changed from its former state is from the majority, and it is like everything that separated from the majority is presumed separated — and the forbidden item, which is the minority, did not change from its former state. So Maharai in Hagahot ShaDa. But one should not say the reason that every fixed item is like half against half, for here before you are two fixed portions — the cut portion and the portion that remained uncut — if so, it is more fitting to say the forbidden is in the cut portion, for this portion is the majority against the second fixed portion. Therefore one must say as Maharai resolved, that the reasoning is that it is in the remaining portion.
9#_: Similar and well aligned. It implies that in appearance they must also be equal; and even though regarding the fat of the gizzard, the appearance of the fat alone suffices, here it is different, since it is possible to clarify also through their being well aligned in cutting — this too must be clarified, in my humble opinion. And Or Zarua wrote in general rule 52: now that we are not so expert, we have no permission to permit in such a case unless there is a great and recognizable difference — end of his words. And Maharshal, may his memory be blessed, wrote, and this is his language: and I received from one scholar who received from the mouths of scholars: if water is found in the head of one sheep that was tereifah in it and it is unknown from which sheep — one should examine the spine-cord of the sheep, and every sheep in which water is found in the brain in the head will have water in the cord extending from the brain to the spine, and we presume that the head is from that sheep to permit the others — end of his words. And in my humble opinion there is nothing worthwhile in this matter to permit a tereifah doubt, since it is not found in the Talmud and poskim.
